What it does: "shaders" are pieces of graphics that the graphics card prepares and saves so it doesn't have to redo them every time. Sometimes, after a driver update, the old ones cause problems. The button deletes them and the game makes new ones.

ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> la scheda video organizz:
What it does: the graphics card organizes its own work instead of being told what to do every time by the processor. The processor has less to do and the image reaches the screen sooner.
When it helps: with recent cards: NVIDIA GTX 10 or newer, AMD RX 7000 or newer, Intel Arc. It's needed for "Frame Generation" (DLSS 3, AFMF). Gain: a little less lag.
Risks: in some old games it can cause small stutters: if so, turn it off. Takes effect after you restart the PC; on old cards Windows ignores it.
ui.<b>Cosa fa:</b> normalmente Windows aspe:
What it does: normally Windows waits a moment and sends data in small batches to save resources. For an online game, it's better for every action (shot, jump, movement) to go out right away. With this, Windows sends everything as soon as it can and doesn't hold the network back.
When it helps: in online games, especially slightly older ones. Gain: a few milliseconds less, but only in games that use this type of connection (mostly MMOs and older games). Modern shooters usually don't, and there nothing changes. Your internet ping doesn't change: that depends on your provider.
Risks: none. Takes effect the next time you start the game.
